outcome: postoperative complications (pyrexia, foul smelling lochia, surgical site infections, uterine tenderness, peritonitis, endometritis)
cohort: 300 pregnant women undergoing emergency or elective caesarean delivery at BLDE (DU) Shri BM Patil Medical College and Research Centre, Vijayapur, Karnataka, India
finding: There was no significant difference in outcomes (side effects, fever, lochia discharge, wound infection, peritonitis) between single and multiple dose antibiotic regimens for preventing infectious morbidity after caesarean delivery.
followup_time: The mean hospital stay was 5 days for non-infectious patients and 10 days for infectious patients.
